title: Nicotine causes brain defects by disrupting the endogenous bioelectric prepattern

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Nicotine causes brain defects by disrupting the endogenous bioelectric prepattern

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors' BETSE model explains nicotine-induced brain defects in Xenopus as resulting from nicotine's disruption of the endogenous bioelectric prepattern (neural tube hyperpolarization) required for brain development.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Nicotine targets Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Our model explains why nicotine induces brain defects: it correctly predicts the disruptive effects of this teratogen on the endogenous bioelectric prepattern required for brain development.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › Nicotine targets Vmem”. Scope: Xenopus laevis neurula and brain development under nicotine exposure

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism has measurable intermediates and interventions, but model fit alone does not establish that Vmem disruption causes the defects. Existing public software and scattered experimental evidence can test parts of the chain, while the full matched dataset is not identified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit competing causal models linking nicotine exposure, neural-tube Vmem contrast, and later brain defects, and test whether disruption of Vmem mediates the exposure effect and whether restoring the contrast rescues morphology.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A causal mediation test needs matched embryo-level voltage and morphology data.

Nicotine has multiple endogenous targets.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.28
operationalizability: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.58
data existence: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The voltage half of the explanation can be rerun in BETSE. The causal half, that this voltage change is why the brain fails, needs the rescue and loss-of-pattern experiments, whose raw scores were not deposited. Published papers from the same group report related Vmem manipulations, which is enough to examine the mechanism on a narrow Xenopus scope and not enough to separate nicotine's other targets. The claim is therefore only partly open to analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Treat the explanation as two results: the model must reduce neural-tube hyperpolarization under nicotine, and brain-defect incidence must track that voltage pattern when voltage is restored or disrupted with nicotine held constant. Failure of the voltage prediction, or defects that persist after the prepattern is restored, would refute the explanation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nicotine has several channel and transcriptional targets, so a voltage correlation is confounded.

Brain-morphology counts for the rescue series are summary bars, not an open embryo table.

Prior Vmem-to-brain papers are separate figures that would have to be compiled by hand.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.62
data existence: 0.38
